sources.name: Kolodziej--Nguyen 1312.5491v2
sources.application: Theorem0.2/2.3 is applied only to two bounded canonical potentials on the compact connected positive Hermitian product H: W is the continuous separated solution and t=max(s,W), with the bounded maximum inequality proved locally in the read GL22 Lemma1.2. For a positive supremum gap, near the infimum of W-(1-epsilon)t the density comparison has factor (1-epsilon)^N exp(lambda M/2)>1 for fixed sufficiently small epsilon. The modified comparison factor 1+C s/epsilon^N tends to one as s tends to zero. Nonempty strict sublevel sets have positive smooth volume by the local submean inequality and q_j is bounded below by 1-alpha>0; W is bounded. Thus the integral used in the contradiction is positive. No global comparison principle or v_-(H)>0 is assumed.

sources.application: Theorem0.1 explicitly allows every lambda>0. The complete Theorem2.1 proof, Lemma2.3 ordering proof, Proposition2.5/Claim2.6 estimates and Corollary2.7 scalar proof were read. The current application is restricted to strictly positive bounded continuous clipped/saturated densities g(y), expressed relative to H^N=b dV; their relative source density is g/b and is in every finite Lp with positive integral. The separated closed-factor zero-exponent solution is continuous with known scalar b/integral g, so Corollary2.7 identifies the unique scalar at those bounded hypotheses. Arbitrary unbounded L1 q_alpha and its limit are handled by the supplied direct construction, not by applying this Lp theorem outside its domain.
